t: Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. No version of the origin of California's name has been fully accepted, but there is wide support for the contention that it derived from an early 16th-century Spanish novel. B. California is a constituent state of the United States of America. C. It was admitted as the 31st state of the union on 9 September 1850 and by the early 1960s it was the most populous U.S. state. D. The influence of the Spanish settlers of the 18th and 19th centuries is evident in California's architecture and place-names.
e: B comes first: it introduces the subject - California is a state of the USA - the broad, general opening statement. A comes next: it introduces an interesting detail about the origin of California's name, expanding on the topic. C comes third: gives historical facts about California's admission to the union and population, continuing the historical information. D comes last: discusses Spanish influence on California's architecture and place names, connecting back to A's mention of the Spanish novel origin and providing a concluding thought. Para Jumble Strategy: 1) Find the opening sentence - usually the most general, introductory statement. 2) Find connectors - pronouns, articles, transition words that link sentences. 3) Find the closing sentence - usually a consequence, conclusion, or summary.

t: Arrange the sentences to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. That magic is believing in yourself a hundred per cent. B. There is only one magic in life that can help you turn your dreams into reality. C. You will be able to face life's challenges with courage only if you believe in yourself and in your capacity to meet those challenges. D. Therefore, the most important lesson that a family can teach its members is to have this faith in oneself.
e: B comes first: introduces the theme - 'there is only one magic in life' - the topic sentence. A comes second: 'That magic is believing in yourself' - the pronoun 'that' links directly back to B's 'one magic.' C comes third: expands on the idea of self-belief and its practical application. D comes last: 'Therefore' signals a conclusion, summarising the lesson for families. Clue Words Used: 'That magic' in A refers back to 'one magic' in B (backward reference); 'Therefore' in D is a conclusion marker.

t: Arrange the sentences to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. In arid regions it may form an almost erect shrub. B. The grape is usually a woody vine, climbing by means of tendrils and often reaching a length of 17 metres or more. C. Small greenish flowers, in clusters, precede the fruit, which varies in colour from almost black to green, red and amber. D. The edible leaves are alternate, palmately lobed and always tooth-edged.
e: B comes first: introduces the subject (the grape) in general terms - the vine's structure - the topic sentence. A comes second: 'it' refers to the grape (from B), describing its form in arid regions - a variation of its typical form. D comes third: describes the leaves, moving from overall plant structure to specific parts. C comes last: describes the flowers and fruit, logically following leaves in the description of the plant's parts. Structure of this paragraph: General → Variation → Parts (leaves) → Parts (flowers/fruit) - a common description pattern in science-related passages.

t: Arrange the sentences to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. On the answer sheet, darken the circle of the correct answer against each question. B. You must select the best answer for each question. C. Every question is followed by four answer choices marked 1, 2, 3 and 4. D. If you darken more than one circle, the answer will be counted as wrong.
e: C comes first: introduces the structure of the question paper (four answer choices) - the starting point of instructions. B comes second: instructs the candidate to select the best answer - the first action to take. A comes third: instructs how to record the answer (darken the circle) - the second action. D comes last: provides a warning about a specific mistake (darkening more than one circle) - naturally the concluding instruction. Logical Sequence: Setup (C) → Action 1 (B) → Action 2 (A) → Warning/Consequence (D).

t: Given below are six sentences. Sentence A is the beginning and F is the last. The middle four are jumbled. Select their correct order: A. We soon ran into a nomad's tent... B. She quickly made us cups of butter tea... C. This time our hostess was a young woman. D. Only then did we notice what a picturesque figure our young hostess made. E. The warmth ran through our frozen bodies... F. She wore a sheepskin cloak...
e: A (scene set) → C (hostess introduced) → B (tea made) → E (warmth felt) → D (noticed her appearance) → F (her description). C introduces hostess, B her action, E effect of warmth, D noticing her appearance — logical narrative flow. Correct order: CBED

t: Given below are six sentences. A is beginning, F is last. Arrange middle four: A. When I studied Engineering thirty-five years back, I was the only girl in the course. B. t: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the correct order: A. I have seen a great many houses in my time...but of one house I have kept a very vivid memory. B. t: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the correct order: A. A fine carriage with rubber tyres...rolled up to the house of a landowner called Gryabov. B. t: Given below are four sentences. Pick the option that gives the correct order: A. The Egyptians believed that the body and soul were important to human existence, in life and in death. B. t: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the correct order: P. Fasting also leads to a feeling of rejuvenation and extended life expectancy. Q. t: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. Though everything was on the up and up for Holzman, yet... something wasn't quite right. B. t: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. Even our own languages A — it that the native speakers hardly B — have contributed words to C — consider foreign anymore
e: The base phrase is "Even our own languages" (given, not to be rearranged). We need to connect the three fragments A, B, C to it logically. Step 1 — Eliminate wrong starting fragments: A cannot be first because it begins with "it" (a pronoun) — there is no antecedent yet; C cannot be first because it begins with "consider" (a verb) without a subject. Step 2 — B must come first: "have contributed words to" is the main verb phrase that follows "Even our own languages" — making it: "Even our own languages have contributed words to..." Step 3 — A follows B: "it that the native speakers hardly" = the pronoun "it" now refers to the words contributed. Step 4 — C completes the sentence: "consider foreign anymore." Complete sentence: "Even our own languages have contributed words to it that the native speakers hardly consider foreign anymore." This means: even words from our own native languages have entered common usage to the extent that native speakers no longer think of them as foreign.

t: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A — He meets me in the same frank friendly way as always without mentioning it. B — He has owed it to me for twelve months now. C — I can realise whenever I meet him that he has forgotten that he owes me a dollar. D — My friend Todd owes me a dollar.
e: The rule for sentence rearrangement is: a sentence that begins with a PRONOUN (He, She, It, They, etc.) CANNOT come first unless the noun it refers to has already been introduced. Step 1 — D must come first: It is the only sentence that introduces the main noun "Todd" and the basic situation (Todd owes a dollar). Sentences A, B, C all start with pronouns (He/I) that refer to Todd and the narrator — so none of them can come first. Step 2 — B follows D: It gives the duration — "He has owed it to me for twelve months now." This adds the time context to the established situation. Step 3 — C follows B: The narrator reflects on the realisation — "I can realise whenever I meet him that he has forgotten he owes me a dollar." Step 4 — A concludes: A describes the observed behaviour — "He meets me in the same frank friendly way as always without mentioning it." Correct order: D → B → C → A = DBCA.

t: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A — On the morning of April 12, Gopal rose at 5.30 am. B — Then he drove to the Joggers Park which was four km away. C — There he met his group of walking enthusiasts. D — He put on his track suit and walking shoes.
e: This paragraph follows a simple chronological morning routine sequence. Step 1 — A must come first: A is the only sentence that introduces the proper noun "Gopal" AND gives the specific time (5:30 am). All other sentences begin with "He" — a pronoun that requires "Gopal" to have been introduced first. Step 2 — D follows A: After waking up, the next logical action is to prepare — "He put on his track suit and walking shoes." One does not drive before getting dressed. Step 3 — B follows D: After dressing, "Then he drove to the Joggers Park which was four km away." Step 4 — C is last: "There he met his group of walking enthusiasts." — "There" refers back to the Joggers Park mentioned in B. Correct order: A → D → B → C = ADBC.

t: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) dreams provide an escape (Q) where reality is suspended (R) into a world (O) of endless possibilities
e: The sentence begins with part (P), "dreams provide an escape," which introduces the subject. Part (R), "into a world," logically follows, describing where this escape leads. Part (O), "of endless possibilities," continues the thought by describing the nature of that world. The sentence then ends with part (Q), "where reality is suspended," which finalizes the description of this imagined world. Reading it together: "Dreams provide an escape into a world of endless possibilities where reality is suspended." Option A (OPQR) breaks the flow by placing "into a world" prematurely; Option C (OQRP) places "where reality is suspended" too early, disrupting the natural progression; Option D (RPOQ) starts with "into a world," which lacks context since nothing has been introduced yet.

t: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. However, new research shows that taking the dog for a walk can have its downsides for seniors. B. Dogs are great companions and provide a healthy excuse to go for a walk and get a bit of exercise. C. It once seemed common sense to believe that having and walking a dog was good for older people. D. A report published in an American medical journal says injuries among seniors related to dog-walking are becoming increasingly prevalent.
e: Sentence C must come first because it is the introductory, standalone statement that presents the general topic ("It once seemed common sense..."). Sentence B comes second because it explains the reasoning behind that common belief — that dogs are good companions for exercise. Sentence A comes third, since it begins with the contrast marker "However," signalling that what follows will challenge the previous claims. Sentence D comes last because it supplies the supporting evidence (the medical journal report) for the contradiction introduced in sentence A. The key strategy for these questions is to look for connector words like "however," "therefore," or "this," which point backward or forward to other sentences in the set, and to identify the one sentence that can stand independently as an opener.

B) Trees help to clean the air we breathe. Through their leaves and bark, they absorb harmful pollutants and release clean oxygen for us to breathe.
C) Increasing levels of carbon dioxide caused by deforestation and fossil fuel combustion trap heat in the atmosphere.
D) In urban environments, trees absorb pollutant gases like nitrogen oxides, ozone, and carbon monoxide, and sweep up particles like dust and smoke.
e:
B and D form the mandatory pair 'BD'. B informs that the trees help in keeping the air that we breathe clean by absorbing harmful pollutants and giving out oxygen in return.
D follows and informs which all pollutant gases the trees absorb in the urban environments.
C and A form another mandatory pair 'CA'. C informs us that there is an issue of increasing levels of carbon dioxide which results in trapped heat in the atmosphere. A informs how the trees act as carbon sinks and counter the effects of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
Pairs BD and CA are present in option (a) only.
So, the correct order is BDCA.
Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
P)  That falling global prices have made imports more feasible — Chicago wheat futures are trading below $260 per tonne, against the $500-plus peaks scaled a year ago — adds to the relative comfort.
Q)   But this isn’t so in milk, where October-March is the “flush” season when buffaloes and cows normally produce more.
R)   The surplus is converted into skimmed milk powder (SMP), butter and ghee by dairies for reconstitution during the “lean” months (April-September), when heat stress and high humidity leads to lower production by animals.
S)   With maximum temperatures not really surging enough to cause yield losses in wheat, concerns over cereal inflation are slowly abating.
e:
B) SPQR 
 S starts the paragraph by setting up the topic of temperature and its impact on wheat yields, which directly addresses concerns about cereal inflation. 
 P follows S, using “That” to connect with the previous idea of cereal inflation. It elaborates on the easing concerns by discussing falling global wheat prices and how imports have become more feasible, reinforcing the context of cereals and inflation. 
 Q logically comes next, introducing a contrasting point with “But” that shifts the focus from cereals to milk. This contrast sets up a new issue by mentioning that, unlike wheat, milk production has a distinct seasonality. 
 R concludes the paragraph by explaining the seasonal dynamics of milk production in more detail. It describes how surplus milk is processed to prepare for the “lean” season, which ties together the discussion about milk production and seasonality.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. 
 A. The review signals GDP will grow close to 7% in 2024-25, with scope to go ‘well above’ 7% by 2030. From about $3.7 trillion this year, India’s economy will expand to $5 trillion in three years, making it the world’s third largest, and could hit the $7 trillion dollar mark by 2030, it reckons. 
 B. Splicing India’s growth story into two phases — 1950-2014, and a ‘decade of transformative growth’ since 2014 — the review stresses that the state of the economy was ‘far from encouraging’ when Prime Minister Narendra Modi ‘assumed power’. 
 C. Ahead of the Interim Budget for 2024-25 on Thursday, the Finance Ministry’s 10-year review of the economy with some forward outlook, serves as a proxy to the annual Economic Survey. 
 D. Post-2014 reforms have restored the economy’s ability to grow healthily with “longer and stronger” economic and financial cycles, and made India the fastest growing G-20 nation, it argues. 
 E. Growth was hobbled by structural constraints such as tardy decision-making, ill-targeted subsidies and a large informal sector, while inflation was unpalatably high.
e:
C) CABED 
 C sets the context with an introductory clause about a significant upcoming event (the Interim Budget) and mentions the 10-year review, providing the necessary introductory information. 
 A uses a forward-looking statement from the review ("The review signals..."), which logically follows the introduction of the review in C. It details specific projections about economic growth, which is a continuation of the topic introduced in C. 
 B introduces a temporal element ("Splicing India’s growth story into two phases") that builds on the growth figures mentioned in A by providing a historical comparison, thus necessitating its placement after A. 
 E describes past challenges ("Growth was hobbled by..."), which elaborates on the historical context introduced in B, explaining what the issues were during the earlier phase. 
 D concludes with the results of reforms ("Post-2014 reforms have restored..."), which is a direct outcome of overcoming the challenges mentioned in E and ties back to the growth and transformation discussed throughout the sequence.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. 
 A. Well, 60 years after Bombay bid adieu to its trams (1964), the passenger tramway in Kolkata, India’s last remaining network, has come to an end 151 years after its introduction. 
 B. Contemporary Turkish playwright, novelist and thinker Mehmet Murat ildan may be a little bit fascinated with trams. 
 C. A small stretch from Maidan to the Esplanade, however, will be retained as a heritage for tram lovers for occasional time-machine rides. 
 D. West Bengal’s administrative authorities contend that trams cause unnecessary congestion on roads that are increasingly difficult to manage. 
 E. He said, “Cities who do not have trams always look less literary, less poetic, and less mysterious!”
e:
C) BEADC 
 Bsentence से paragraph की शुरुआत होती है क्योंकि इसमें Mehmet Murat Ildan का परिचय दिया गया है, जो एक Turkish playwright, novelist, और thinker हैं। इसमें बताया गया है कि Ildan ट्रामों के प्रति काफी fascinated हैं। 
 E logically Bके बाद आता है क्योंकि इसमें Mehmet Murat Ildan का quote दिया गया है, जिसमें वह कहते हैं कि जिन शहरों में ट्राम नहीं होतीं, वे कम “literary, poetic, and mysterious” लगते हैं। यह ट्रामों के poetic और symbolic महत्व को highlight करता है। 
 A, Eके बाद आता है क्योंकि यह ट्रामों के संदर्भ को India से जोड़ता है। यह बताता है कि Bombay में ट्राम का अंत हो गया था और Kolkata में 151 साल बाद आखिरकार ट्राम नेटवर्क बंद हो गया, जो भारत का आखिरी बचा हुआ ट्राम नेटवर्क था। यह ट्राम के इतिहास और वर्तमान स्थिति को विस्तार से बताता है। 
 Dइसके बाद आता है क्योंकि यह West Bengal’s authorities का दृष्टिकोण बताता है, जो मानते हैं कि ट्रामें सड़कों पर “congestion” का कारण बनती हैं और उन्हें manage करना मुश्किल हो जाता है। यह ट्रामों के decline का practical कारण देता है। 
 C paragraphको conclude करता है, यह बताते हुए कि Maidan से Esplanade तक एक छोटा हिस्सा heritage के रूप में रखा जाएगा ताकि tram lovers कभी-कभी इस historical ride का आनंद ले सकें। यह पूरे paragraph को एक nostalgic और thoughtful conclusion देता है। 
 Explanation in English: 
 B + E:B introduces the subject (Mehmet Murat Ildan), and E gives his quote. The subject (Mehmet Murat Ildan) is continued from B into E through “he said.” 
 E + A:A shifts the focus from Ildan’s opinion to a factual statement about trams in India. A directly connects with E by continuing the discussion about trams but now focusing on the real-life situation in Kolkata. 
 A + D:D follows A by explaining why trams were discontinued, connecting the factual situation in A with the reasoning in D. 
 D + C:C provides a contrast to D by giving an exception to the closure. It connects by showing that despite the closure, a small stretch will be retained for heritage purposes.

The middle four sentences have been jumbled and labelled P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your answer accordingly.
S1: The cosmos, with its mystery governed by immutable laws of poetic precision, staggered her imagination
S6:. And so, at seventeen, she founded a small school of her own.
P : by fifteen, she had mastered higher mathematics
Q : which she supplemented with an ardent love of poetry
R : further to offer her in the way of higher education for a woman
S : no institution - not on the island, not on the globe - had anything
The proper sequence should be
e:
The first and the last sentence are fixed. We need to arrange PQRS in a way that the arrangement is meaningful and grammatically correct.
The last sentence (S6) mentions that 'so, she opened her own school'. The use of 'so' gives us a hint that the reason for her opening her own school must have been mentioned somewhere and it should precede the last sentence. The reason is mentioned in SR in that order; the reason being that no institution had anything to offer her. Option C satisfies this criterion. And PQSR is a meaningful sentence arrangement. Option C is the correct answer.

t:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This profound philosophy treats breakage and repair as an integral part of the history of an object, rather than as something to be shamefully disguised.
B. Kintsugi is the exquisite Japanese art of repairing broken pottery by mending the areas of breakage with lacquer dusted or mixed with powdered gold or silver.
C. Consequently, the repaired ceramic piece is often considered more beautiful and valuable than the original, as it proudly showcases its scars as a mark of resilience.
D. Instead of attempting to hide the cracks, this unique method deliberately highlights them, celebrating imperfection as a beautiful part of the object's unique journey through time.
e: The correct sequence is BADC. Sentence B serves as the ideal introduction by defining the subject, "Kintsugi," and explaining the basic technique. Sentence A builds upon this by explaining the "profound philosophy" behind the art form mentioned in B. Sentence D elaborates on "this unique method" by contrasting it with typical repair, emphasizing how it "deliberately highlights" the cracks, which directly follows the philosophical point in A. Sentence C, with its transition word "Consequently," provides the logical conclusion, explaining the result of this artistic and philosophical approach, that the repaired piece becomes more beautiful. Hence, option (c) is the answer.

t:
A sentence has been split up into segments and given below in jumbled order. While the first and the last segments of the sentence (1 and 6) are in the correct order, the segments in between are jumbled up. Arrange the segments in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.
1) India has been a land
P) and the learned man has been held in higher esteem
Q) of learning through the ages
R) but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued
S) not indeed in the sense that education has been universal
6) than the warrior or the administrator.
e:
The sentence starts with "India has been a land" and ends with "than the warrior or the administrator." The middle segments must describe India's relationship with learning. Starting with Q, "of learning through the ages," defines the land. Then, S, "not indeed in the sense that education has been universal," clarifies the nature of learning. Next, R, "but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued," contrasts with S. Finally, P, "and the learned man has been held in higher esteem," connects to the ending.
The order Q-S-R-P forms: "India has been a land of learning through the ages, not indeed in the sense that education has been universal, but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued, and the learned man has been held in higher esteem than the warrior or the administrator."
Option 2 is correct.

t:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Remote work and flexible schedules have become more common, allowing employees to achieve a better work-life balance. 
B. This shift has also opened up new opportunities for people with disabilities, caregivers, and those living in remote areas, promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workforce.
C. The future of work is evolving rapidly, influenced by technological advancements and changing workforce dynamics. 
D. As a result, productivity and job satisfaction have increased, leading to improved overall well-being for workers.
e:
The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is CADB.
Sentence C introduces the topic by stating that "The future of work is evolving rapidly," setting the context for discussing changes in work dynamics.
Sentence A follows by detailing one specific change: "Remote work and flexible schedules have become more common, allowing employees to achieve a better work-life balance." This sentence builds on the theme of evolving work dynamics presented in C. Accordingly, CA forms a logical pair. 
Sentence D then explains the positive outcomes of these changes: "As a result, productivity and job satisfaction have increased, leading to improved overall well-being for workers." This shows the effects of remote work and flexible schedules mentioned in A.
Sentence B concludes the paragraph by expanding on the implications of these changes, noting that this shift has opened up new opportunities for underrepresented groups, thus promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion. This ties back to the evolving nature of work while emphasising its broader social impact. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

t:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
Jobseekers are not
P. being unemployed are a test of faith
Q. self-purification, where the difficulties of
R. relentlessly to a pilgrimage of
S. fatalistic but reapply themselves
e: The correct order is SRQP. The phrase P mentions the plural verb 'are'. Therefore, it must agree with a plural noun. Q mentions the plural noun 'difficulties'. The pair QP is grammatically and contextually correct. Phrase R mentions the adverb 'relentlessly' (in an unceasingly intense or harsh way). It should qualify a verb/adjective/adverb. It can be used to qualify the verb 'reapply'. Therefore, the pair SR is grammatically and contextually correct. Using these pairs, we can conclude that option (c) is the correct answer. The correct sentence after rearrangement is: Jobseekers are not fatalistic but reapply themselves relentlessly to a pilgrimage of self-purification, where the difficulties of being unemployed are a test of faith.

t:
In the following question, the first and the last sentence are given marked as S1 and S6 respectively. Other parts have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the sentences and mark your answer accordingly.

S1: Over the past century, cooking techniques have evolved and diversified, and cooking has started to move away from more primitive heat sources.
S6: Increasingly, scientists have been pointing to the microwave as a healthier way of cooking - depending on what you cook in it.
P. microwaves, electric hobs and toasters can
Q. now be found in almost
R. an alternative to high flames
S. every house, providing
e:
S1 talks about the evolution of cooking techniques and the movement away from 'primitive heat sources', and S6 puts forward scientists' views of healthier ways of cooking in a microwave. We need sentence(s) that can connect these two ideas. P talks about the alternative heat sources (heat sources are mentioned in S1) that have been adopted, i.e. 'microwaves, electric hobs, and toasters'. Q carries the sentence forward by talking about where these devices are commonly used, and the answer lies in S (i.e., almost 'every house'). R completes the sentence by tagging these sources as alternatives to high flames. Thus, the correct order is PQSR.
Hence, c) is the correct answer.

t:
Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

S1. In today's interconnected world, 
A. and unparalleled access to a vast array 
B. communication, global information exchange 
C. of knowledge, transforming the way
D. the internet facilitates instant 
S6. we live and interreact.
e: S1 introduces the context of the interconnected world and sets the tone for the paragraph. Part D provides a specific aspect of the interconnected world, focusing on the internet's role in enabling instant communication. Part D is followed by part B because it elaborates on the idea of communication introduced in part D. Also, 'instant' in part D is an adjective and would appropriately be followed by the noun 'communication' in part B. So, DB is a mandatory pair. Part B mentions the global exchange of information, further expanding on the topic. Part B leads to part A as it provides additional information about the global exchange of information, which includes unparalleled access to a wide variety of knowledge. Part A naturally flows into part C as it talks about unparalleled access to knowledge. Part C then discusses how this access to knowledge is transforming the way things work. The sentence concludes with S6, which summarizes the overall impact of the interconnected world on the way we live and interact. Rearranging parts in the order of DBAC forms a coherent sentence. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. The final sentence would be: In today's interconnected world, the internet facilitates instant communication, global information exchange, and unparalleled access to a vast array of knowledge, transforming the way we live and interact.

t:
Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence. 

S1) A fasting glucose tolerance test 
A) from an impairment of sugar metabolism, 
B) about decreased tolerance to sugar 
C) in persons suffering 
D) can convey important information 
S6) such as diabetes mellitus.
e:
The correct order to form a coherent paragraph/sentence is DBCA. S1 introduces the topic of the fasting glucose tolerance test. Part D follows the introduction of the test and emphasises the significance of the test by highlighting its ability to provide important information. Part B logically follows, explaining one of the key aspects evaluated during the test - decreased tolerance to sugar. Part C provides context by specifying that the test applies to individuals who are suffering from a certain condition. Part A follows part C as it names the condition (an impairment of sugar metabolism). Finally, S6 concludes the paragraph by giving an example of the condition that the fasting glucose tolerance test can detect - diabetes mellitus. 
Part A ("from an impairment of sugar metabolism") and S6 ("such as diabetes mellitus") form a logical pair because they complement each other. Part A names a condition/health issue and S6 gives an example of that condition. In option (c), part A is placed at last to form a pair with S6. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.
The sentence formed is: A fasting glucose tolerance test can convey important information about decreased tolerance to sugar in persons suffering from an impairment of sugar metabolism, such as diabetes mellitus.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Farmers can have multiple harvests to supplement their income.
B. Though known to be highly nutritious and still consumed but in a limited quantity, it has economic benefits too.
C. Efforts are under way to popularise the inclusion of Amaranthus - a wide variety of leafy vegetables. 
D. But cultivation was gradually on the wane and with it a slice of culinary culture.
e: Sentence C comes first as it introduces us to the main subject of the passage 'Amaranthus'. B follows C as it states that this leafy vegetable is nutritious and profitable. A follows B as it states that farmers can have multiple harvests of Amaranthus as it is profitable. 'But' is used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned. Although the vegetable provides a good income, cultivation was decreased (says sentence D). So, this can be a concluding sentence of the passage. Therefore, CBAD becomes the correct order among the given options. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t:
Given below are six sentences, out of which sentences A and F are in the correct positions. Sentences B, C, D and E are in jumbled order. Select the option that gives the correct order. 

A. Urban policy experts have long been arguing that the existing railway infrastructure in the state cannot meet the demands of the future.
B. The government claims the MONO project can take a significant load of traffic off. 
C. This will make travel faster for commuters and reduce congestion on roads.
D. Most trains run at an average speed of 45 km/hr due to a lot of curves and bends on the existing stretch.
E. The state government began the process of land acquisition after the state's cabinet approval in June 2021.
F. Out of 1,383 hectares needed to be acquired, 1,198 hectares will be private land.
e:
The correct order is: ADBCEF.
The first sentence states that the current railway infrastructure cannot meet the demands of the future. D follows A as it talks about the reason for this. Therefore, AD is a pair. Sentence B follows and introduces us to the MONO project. It states that the project can take a significant load of traffic off. C follows B as it talks about the advantages of the project. The last sentence talks about land acquisition. Sentence E also talks about land acquisition. So, E precedes F.
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

A. Consumption of food prepared
B. An important food-related 
C. Is the increase in 
D. Lifestyle change of the past two decades 
E. Away from home
e: The correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence is BDCAE. Part B comes first as it sets the context that the sentence will discuss something related to food. Part D follows logically because it specifies what kind of change or trend related to food is being discussed. It introduces the main topic of the sentence, which is the change in lifestyle over the past two decades (Accordingly, BD forms a logical pair). Part C logically follows D because it continues the thought about the lifestyle change introduced in D. It suggests that there has been an increase in something related to this change. Part A then specifies what has increased (consumption of food) as mentioned in C. It talks about the consumption of food that is prepared in a certain manner or location. Part E concludes the sentence by specifying where the food is prepared (away from home). Hence, (a) is the correct answer. The complete sentence is: An important food-related lifestyle change of the past two decades is the increase in consumption of food prepared away from home.

t:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Often referred to as the "rainforests of the sea," coral reefs are incredibly diverse underwater ecosystems built by colonies of tiny animals called coral polyps.
B. These vibrant structures provide essential habitats for approximately twenty-five percent of all marine species, making them one of the most biodiverse environments on the planet.
C. However, these vital ecosystems are currently facing unprecedented threats from climate change, pollution, and destructive fishing practices that cause widespread coral bleaching.
D. Each individual polyp secretes a calcium carbonate exoskeleton, and over thousands of years, these exoskeletons accumulate to form the massive structures we see today.
e: The correct sequence is ADBC. Sentence A is the ideal opening sentence as it defines "coral reefs" and introduces the "coral polyps" that build them. Sentence D logically follows by explaining exactly how "Each individual polyp" (mentioned in A) contributes to building the "massive structures" of the reef. Sentence B then describes the immense ecological importance of "These vibrant structures" (the reefs from A and D), highlighting their role in supporting marine life. Finally, sentence C introduces a contrasting point with the word "However," shifting the focus to the "unprecedented threats" that "these vital ecosystems" are facing, which serves as a poignant conclusion. Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. Perhaps he helped turn their home into a saint arcade by requisitioning church overstock; but by any measure, it was quite a display.
B. There had to be six or seven larger-than-kid-sized statues on the second-floor landing, right at the top of the stairs.
C. Uncle John, now late in life, worked part-time as a janitor for our parish.
D. There they stood, in various poses of melancholy, misery, piety and/or penance, hands beckoning, in two-finger blessings with thumb and ring finger circled, or else holding something significant to each.
e: The correct sequence of the sentences will be: C. Uncle John, now late in life, worked part-time as a janitor for our parish. A. Perhaps he helped turn their home into a saint arcade by requisitioning church overstock; but by any measure, it was quite a display. B. There had to be six or seven larger-than-kid-sized statues on the second-floor landing, right at the top of the stairs. D. There they stood, in various poses of melancholy, misery, piety and/or penance, hands beckoning, in two-finger blessings with thumb and ring finger circled, or else holding something significant to each. Identifying the first sentence in the paragraph is a basic step to solve the para jumble. Among the given sentences, C can be easily identified as the introductory sentence as it introduces us to Uncle John, who is old and used to work part-time as a cleaner for the author's parish. A is in continuation of C as it tells us more about Uncle John. It is mentioned that maybe he assisted in the transformation of their home into a saint arcade by obtaining church leftovers, but it was an impressive show in any case. Thereafter, B carries forward the paragraph as it gives us the details of the figures or statues brought from the church by Uncle John. On the second floor, just at the top of the stairs, there had to be six or seven big sculptures. D is the concluding sentence as it mentions the characteristics of the statues - already talked about in B. Therefore, the correct answer is: (b) CABD.

t:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. As the tide moves in and out along the shoreline, the organisms in these areas undergo drastic changes in temperature, moisture, and salinity levels within short intervals.
B. Intertidal zones, which occur along various coastlines across the globe, are unique areas that remain submerged during high tide and become exposed at low tide.
C. This dynamic and challenging environment supports a diverse range of species that have evolved to cope with rapid and extreme fluctuations in their surroundings.
D. Crabs, mussels, barnacles, and sea stars are just a few examples of the many inhabitants that possess specialized adaptations to endure this ever-changing habitat.
e: The correct sequence is BCAD. Sentence B introduces the topic by clearly explaining what intertidal zones are, making it the appropriate starting point. Sentence C naturally follows by elaborating on the unique biodiversity supported by such zones. Sentence A provides a deeper insight into the environmental challenges these organisms face daily. Sentence D then concludes by giving concrete examples of creatures that live in these conditions and how they survive. This structure builds logically from definition, to explanation, to challenges, and finally to examples. Hence, option (b) is the answer.

A. Prompting the move was the observation of a chef, who reached out to the museum last year to bring to its notice that the foreground of the painting did not depict onions. 
B. Almost 135 years after it was painted by Vincent van Gogh, the artwork Red Cabbages and Onions has now been rechristened Red Cabbages and Garlic.

A follows B as it talks about why the museum renamed the painting. Sentence C, obviously is the continuation of sentence A as it builds up on A. The remaining sentence D is the last part of the passage.

t:
A sentence, split into four parts, has been given. Choose the best order which produces the original sentence. 
achieving such a feat(A)/ an elite club of nations(B)/ would see India enter(C)/ a successful mission(D)
e:
The correct order is DCBA.
Part D introduces the condition or outcome of a successful mission, highlighting the importance of achieving success.
Part C describes the consequence or effect of a successful mission, stating that it would lead to India entering or joining something.
Part B specifies the group or category that India would become a part of, emphasizing it as an elite club of nations.
Part A provides additional information about the accomplishment or achievement, highlighting that the nations in the elite club have achieved a similar feat.
By arranging these parts in the given order, the sentence forms a coherent and meaningful statement.
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. 
The rearranged sentence is: A successful mission would see India enter an elite club of nations achieving such a feat.

t:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. These kinds of sharks are known as obligate ram ventilators because they draw water in through their mouths and force it out through their gills.
B. They use a method called buccal pumping, in which water is pulled in through the mouth and forced out through the gills by the cheek muscles.
C. It is true that many types of sharks must keep moving in order to receive life-giving oxygen from the water passing through their gills.
D. Other types of sharks are able to remain stationary because they possess special structures called spiracles, which force water out through their gills.
e:
'C' is the first sentence as it introduces the main subject 'types of sharks', it is followed by 'A' as it gives a name to the types of sharks mentioned in 'C'. How they breathe is mentioned in 'A' and what the whole process is called (i.e. buccal pumping), is mentioned in 'B'. 'D' is the final sentence as it talks about the other types of sharks that are stationary, so it is an independent sentence and can be used at the end of the paragraph. Therefore, the correct order of rearrangement is CABD.
Hence, option (a) is correct.

t:
Some parts of a sentence have been jumbled up, and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.
Embracing acceptance 
P) cultivates a culture of openness and tolerance 
Q) for who they are, 
R) that fosters a community 
S) where people are embraced 
regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity.
e:
The correct sequence to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence is PRSQ. Part P introduces the result or outcome of "Embracing acceptance." It describes what happens as a consequence of embracing acceptance, which is the development of a culture characterised by openness and tolerance. Part R connects to the previous part by explaining the purpose or impact of the culture of openness and tolerance mentioned earlier. It states that this culture serves as a foundation or environment that supports the creation or development of a community. Parts S and Q further explain the nature of the community. They describe that in the community, people are welcomed or accepted for who they are. This implies that people are accepted as it is, regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity. The correct sequence (PRSQ) maintains a logical flow in the sentence structure by first introducing the result of embracing acceptance (cultivating openness and tolerance), explaining how this culture fosters a community, and finally describing the inclusive nature of that community where individuals are embraced regardless of their background or beliefs. This arrangement forms a coherent and meaningful sentence describing the positive effects of embracing acceptance. 
The sentence formed is: Embracing acceptance cultivates a culture of openness and tolerance that fosters a community where people are embraced for who they are, regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity.
Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(a) encourage individuals to seek timely support,
(b) raising awareness about mental health issues
(c) and foster a more compassionate
(d) helps to reduce stigma,
(e) and understanding society overall
e: (b) Raising awareness about mental health issues - This gerund phrase serves as the subject of the sentence, introducing the main action being discussed. (d) helps to reduce stigma, - This is the main verb phrase ("helps") for the subject in (b), followed by the first benefit or outcome ("to reduce stigma"). So far: "Raising awareness about mental health issues helps to reduce stigma," (a) encourage individuals to seek timely support, - This infinitive phrase (with "to" implied from "helps to") presents the second benefit, parallel in structure to "reduce stigma." It logically follows (d): "...helps to reduce stigma, encourage individuals to seek timely support," (c) and foster a more compassionate - This phrase, beginning with "and," introduces the third benefit, continuing the list of positive outcomes. The verb "foster" is also parallel. Now: "...encourage individuals to seek timely support, and foster a more compassionate" (e) and understanding society overall - This completes the description of the type of society fostered, with "and understanding" being parallel to "compassionate." It forms the object of "foster." Final sentence: "Raising awareness about mental health issues helps to reduce stigma, encourage individuals to seek timely support, and foster a more compassionate and understanding society overall." Hence, option (d) is the answer.

t:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.
(P) for maintaining ecological balance
(Q) and safeguarding numerous unique species
(O) protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial
(R) from extinction
e: The sentence begins effectively with part (O) "Protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial". The gerund phrase "Protecting biodiversity hotspots" acts as the subject, and "is crucial" is the predicate, establishing the main idea. Part (P) "for maintaining ecological balance" is a prepositional phrase that explains why protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial, stating the first reason or purpose. So far: "Protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial for maintaining ecological balance". Part (Q) "and safeguarding numerous unique species" introduces a second, parallel reason, connected by the conjunction "and." It continues the explanation of the importance stated in (O). Part (R) "from extinction" is a prepositional phrase that modifies "safeguarding numerous unique species," specifying what they are being safeguarded from. It completes the idea in (Q). Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is OPQR. The sentence formed after rearrangement is: Protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial for maintaining ecological balance and safeguarding numerous unique species from extinction. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

A. However, with the global population expected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, the need for sustainable food production will only intensify. 
B. The focus on reducing food waste and promoting sustainable agriculture is not just a matter of environmental responsibility but also a critical step towards ensuring global food security.

D. The world is currently facing an unprecedented challenge: to feed a rapidly growing population while addressing environmental concerns like climate change.
e:

Sentence A, which introduces the contradiction to the information in B must be the last sentence, thereby concluding the paragraph. So, the possible arrangements are CDBA and DCBA.

t:
Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (A and F) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

A. The athlete's
B. shattered records
C. incredible performance
D. established a new benchmark
E. and
F. in their respective sport.
e: The correct order is ACBEDF. The sentence begins with the possessive phrase "The athlete's", indicating that something belongs to the athlete. It is to be followed by the noun phrase "incredible performance", describing what the athlete did. The phrase "shattered records" describes the result or consequence of the performance, indicating that existing records were broken. The conjunction "and" connects the two parts of the sentence. The phrase "established a new benchmark" describes another result of the performance, indicating that a new standard was set. Lastly, the prepositional phrase "in their respective sport" specifies the specific domain or field in which the records were shattered, and the benchmark was established. By arranging these parts in the given order, the sentence forms a coherent and meaningful statement. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer. The rearranged sentence is: The athlete's incredible performance shattered records and established a new benchmark in their respective sport. Note: Prepositional phrase: A modifying phrase consisting of a preposition and its object. Example: The cat was hiding under the table. Here, 'under' is the preposition while 'table' is its object. Possessive nouns are types of nouns that show ownership or connection. All nouns become possessive nouns with the addition of an apostrophe and a suffix - the letter "s" - at the end of the word. However, when a plural noun ends in the letter "s," the possessive form of the word only requires the use of an apostrophe at the end. Possessive nouns can be tricky because they function like adjectives by modifying another noun or pronoun in the sentence. E.g., "Timmy's dog is cute." Noun phrase: A noun phrase is built around a single noun. Example: Their website published an article about the importance of focused work. Here 'article' is a noun and the part highlighted is a noun phrase.

t:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Identify the options that arrange the part in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. 
A. It took two days
B. who had set out
C. spotted by one of his
D. for him to be
E. fellow fishermen
F. to search for him
e: In all the options, A is the first part, and F is the last part. Only phrase D can follow A. The preposition 'for' connects the purpose of those two days. 'To be' is followed by a participle verb. Therefore, only C can follow D because 'spotted' here will be the past participle. 'His' is a possessive determiner which requires a noun after it. So, the phrase 'fellow fisherman' can follow C. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the subject of the sentence/clause (living things). So, B follows E. The correct order is ADCEBF. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. The correct sentence is: It took two days for him to be spotted by one of his fellow fishermen who had set out to search for him. Note: "Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below: Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground. Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion. The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect. The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of. A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n. One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective." Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books." Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

Sentence D concludes the paragraph and provides relatable context, mentioning the common observation and study of these microbes in schools, specifically noting their visibility through a microscope. This sequence offers a coherent flow, initiating with an introduction to microbes beyond bacteria, discussing the diversity of microscopic organisms, delving into their roles and distinctions, exploring specific types of eukaryotic microbes, and concluding with a relatable context of their study and observation. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

Note: Relative Clause: A relative clause is one that's connected to the main clause of the sentence by a word such as who, whom, which, that, or whose. t:
Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (A and F) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

A. The newly discovered exoplanet
B. could potentially support
C. making it
D. a significant find
E. life
F. in the search for extraterrestrial habitats.
e: The correct order is ABECDF. The sentence begins with the subject "The newly discovered exoplanet", referring to the recently found planet. Then it states that the exoplanet "could potentially support" something, which is "life" in this case. The introductory phrase "making it" introduces the reason or explanation for the significance of the exoplanet. It is followed by the noun phrase "a significant find", emphasizing the importance of the discovery. Lastly, the prepositional phrase "in the search for extraterrestrial habitats" specifies the domain or context in which the exoplanet's significance lies. By arranging these parts in the given order, the sentence forms a coherent and meaningful statement. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. The rearranged sentence is: The newly discovered exoplanet could potentially support life, making it a significant find in the search for extraterrestrial habitats. Note: Prepositional phrase: A modifying phrase consisting of a preposition and its object. Example: The cat was hiding under the table. Here, 'under' is the preposition while 'table' is its object. Noun phrase: A noun phrase is built around a single noun. Example: Their website published an article about the importance of focused work. Here 'article' is a noun and the part highlighted is a noun phrase.
